one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent successfully built the kernel and initramfs but failed to verify the QEMU boot output due to repeated QEMU invocation errors including grep-gating that blocked execution, insufficient timeouts (10-30s), and final error masking with '|| true', then prematurely submitted completion without any confirmed serial output.
t_err_evidence: grep -a -m1 'Hello, this is a custom kernel' linux-6.9/vmlinux && ... timeout 12s qemu-system-x86_64 ...
t_commit_evidence: After step 16, all remaining steps (17-21) continue the same flawed QEMU invocation pattern (too-short timeouts of 20s, 10s, 15s, 30s; grep-gating that blocks execution; final '|| true' masking) with no successful boot output ever obtained; the agent claims completion at step 21 without any QEMU serial output.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks knowledge of two things: (1) the typical boot time for a freshly built kernel in QEMU exceeds 20-30 seconds before serial printk output appears, causing repeated timeout failures; (2) binary grep on a large vmlinux may fail to find the string (due to symbol encoding/compression), so chaining QEMU behind grep returns non-zero and silently blocks QEMU from ever running.
